subject: Re: Concurrency requirements & Redwood rate limits — follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Concurrency requirements & Redwood rate limits — post-call recap

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate: 

Summary of your targets (as discussed)
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 400 ms for conversational traffic (average response ~120 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained ~250 requests/sec for core flows during business hours; peaks up to ~700 requests/sec for promotional spikes.
- Concurrency: up to 500 parallel inference requests system-wide; typical per-connection concurrency ~10.
- Streaming: chat UI requires chunked/streaming responses for best UX.

Open questions we agreed to clarify:
1) Do you have strict per-user concurrency limits (e.g., connection pooling requirements)?
2) Expected token-per-minute budget per account (billing and quota sizing).
3) Tolerance for fallbacks (e.g., slower model variant under heavy load) vs. required hard guarantees.

What Redwood can do (short):
- Hosted rate-limit flexibility: we can provision temporary burst capacity and adjust quotas per account.
- Dedicated option: for sustained high concurrency and guaranteed throughput we recommend Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools).
- Connection strategies: we support HTTP/2 multiplexing and WebSocket-based streaming; we can also advise on client-side connection pooling to keep active connections within limits.

Proposed next steps:
- Alex to send a short traffic sample CSV (per-endpoint RPS, peak windows) — you mentioned you could provide this.
- I'll loop in Neha (solutions/SRE) to propose a concrete rate-limit/quota matrix and recommended connection configuration.
- We will provide a draft SLA/quote and a mutual action plan with milestones.

Attaching a lightweight template for the traffic sample and next steps. Happy to jump back on a quick tech call with your SREs next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency requirements & Redwood rate limits — post-call recap

Thanks, Marissa — this is helpful. I attached the traffic sample you requested (acme-traffic-sample.csv). A few clarifications from our side: 

- Per-user concurrency: most users open a single chat session but our mobile clients may open up to 3 concurrent requests per user (background checks + active chat). We don't want per-user hard limits right now, but we do need good connection pooling guidance so we don't overwhelm devices.
- Token budget: estimate ~25M tokens/day initially, ramping to ~100M over 3 months if the pilot is successful.
- Streaming: streaming is required for chat experiences — low latency chunks are important.
- Fallbacks: acceptable as long as there is clear degradation (e.g., switch to smaller model with notice) and no silent failures.

Can Neha propose a concrete rate-limit/quota matrix based on the attached sample? Also please include an estimate for monthly hosted usage vs. Dedicated baseline for comparison.

Best,
Alex
Alex Jones, Head of Product
Acme Payments
alex.jones@acme.com

Attachment: acme-traffic-sample.csv (3 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency requirements & Redwood rate limits — post-call recap

Appreciate the sample, Alex — that's exactly what we need. Looping in Neha (our SRE/solutions lead) to propose a rate-limit matrix and specific connection recommendations.

Quick answers while Neha crafts the matrix:
- For streaming chat: we recommend HTTP/2 or WebSocket streaming to avoid repeated connection setup. WebSockets give the smoothest chunked UX.
- Client pooling: advise keeping 6-8 pooled connections per host for mobile; desktop can sustain higher multiplexing via HTTP/2.
- Token budgeting: we'll translate your token/day into average tokens/sec and map that against model throughput to estimate monthly bill and CPU/GPU pressure.

Next: Neha will propose a tiered rate-limit plan (baseline / burst / emergency) and a recommended Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparison. I'll also draft a short mutual action plan and attach the initial SLA/quote.

Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed rate-limit matrix & connection guidance

Alex — reviewed the traffic sample. High level recommendations below; I attached a more detailed spreadsheet (rate-limit-matrix.xlsx) with per-endpoint suggestions and fallback rules.

Recommended baseline quotas (hosted)
- Baseline: 300 rps sustained (system-wide), per-account token cap mapped to ~30M tokens/month.
- Burst: up to 900 rps for short windows (up to 10 minutes) with token throttling above baseline.
- Emergency: reserved failover lane (lower-cost model variant) if sustained >900 rps for >30 minutes.

Concurrency & connection pooling
- We suggest client-side pooling at 6 pooled connections per mobile client and leveraging HTTP/2 multiplexing for desktop to keep active TCP connections low.
- For server-side parallelism, treat the 500 parallel requests target as aggressive for hosted; if you expect sustained >300 parallel active model inferences, we strongly recommend Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) for predictable latency and throughput.

Streaming vs non-streaming
- Streaming increases connection time but reduces perceived latency. We size capacity assuming a 2-3x connection duration for streaming flows vs non-streaming.

SLOs and fallbacks
- To meet your p95 <= 400 ms target under hosted with mixed traffic, we'll need either (a) conservative request routing to heavier SKU models, or (b) Dedicated with pinned capacity.

Next steps
1) We'll propose a rate-limit/quota matrix in the attached spreadsheet and mark recommended tiers for your pilot.
2) Marissa will follow up with a draft SLA and quote.
3) If you want a Dedicated quote, we need a short sizing call (30 min) to confirm peak concurrency windows and token mix.

Attachment: rate-limit-matrix.xlsx (12 KB)

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>

Thanks, Neha — that matrix looks reasonable based on our expected traffic. Two asks before we move forward: 

1) Procurement is asking for a formal quote and an SLA exception for the burst lanes (we need documented uptime and latency SLOs during bursts).
2) We want a 90-day pilot with an option to convert to Dedicated if sustained >300 parallel inferences. Please include pilot pricing and the trigger terms in the quote.

Procurement (copied) — can you confirm any additional legal/PO requirements? We can get the traffic and billing contacts to finalize.

Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Alex / Procurement —

Great — we’ll get a formal quote and draft SLA over to you by end of day tomorrow. Items we will include:
- Pilot pricing (90-day) with baseline quotas and defined burst lanes.
- SLA language for latency SLOs during baseline; documented fallback behavior for burst lanes with an explicit escalation path.
- Trigger terms for Dedicated conversion (sustained >300 parallel inferences for 7 consecutive days or consistent token burn >2x baseline for 30 days).
- Actions: DocuSign link for pilot agreement, a HubSpot mutual action plan (link included), and the rate-limit spreadsheet attached.

We’ll target a 30-minute sizing call this week to size Dedicated if you want that option included. Marcus / Neha will be on that call to confirm the concurrency math.

Thanks — attaching the first draft SLA and the rate-limit matrix for your review.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference
